name: Ellen Randall
life: “I still remember a taxi window stuck shut with four passengers inside.” People around Maré Coffee know Ellen by a small Thursday habit. Ellen likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I can help if nobody smokes in the car. Asking made me feel more fragile than giving lifts.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an old plum windbreaker and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Ellen has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. Ellen presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Ellen thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Ellen sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To keep the shared van smoke-free.
family: Gavin Jones is Ellen’s second cousin. Ellen sets the time to leave. Gavin picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The free fringe*, Gavin says, “I was the next in line and angry. The customer gave me a ride to my interview when our time ran over.”
connections: Bianca Spencer. The no-smoking driver agrees to handle fuel money out of the rider's children's hearing.

reactions.situation: A shift worker is late to the meeting point
reactions.response: Ellen checks whether waiting will make the whole shift late and tells the rider the decision.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Ellen gets the people at the next doorway away from the smoke and asks a bystander to make the call.
